name: MonarchAiWelcome
title: AiWelcome
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column (centered) with MonarchAiAgentAvatar, androidx.compose.material3.Text headings and slots for MonarchAiStarterPrompts and MonarchAiDisclaimer
summary: The empty state of a new conversation: the assistant's avatar, name and role, a greeting, what it can help with, starting points and a footer.
whenToUse: As the empty content of a conversation, before the first message, to say who answers and where to start.
whenNotToUse: For an empty list that is not a conversation, use MonarchEmptyState. For starting points alone, use MonarchAiStarterPrompts.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiWelcome(title: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef? = null, agentImage: Painter? = null, description: String? = null, capabilities: List<String> = emptyList(), icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, capabilityIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, capabilitiesLabel: String? = null, agentPrefix: String? = null, footer: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, starters: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The greeting, such as How can I help?. Read as a heading.

options.name: agent
options.description: The assistant answering in this conversation. Shows its MonarchAiAgentAvatar, name and role; without it an AI mark is shown.

options.name: agentImage
options.description: The agent's picture. Monarch loads no images; load MonarchAiAgentRef.avatar in the app.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on what the assistant can see or do, in muted text.

options.name: capabilities
options.description: Short capability statements, shown as a checklist aligned to the start.

options.name: icon
options.description: An AI glyph in the mark shown without an agent, tinted in the AI strong color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: capabilityIcon
options.description: A check mark before each capability, tinted in the muted color. Without it a small dot is drawn.

options.name: capabilitiesLabel
options.description: Replaces the spoken name of the capabilities, What I can help with (monarch_aiwelcome_capabilities).

options.name: agentPrefix
options.description: Replaces the spoken prefix before the agent's name, AI assistant: (monarch_aiwelcome_agent_prefix).

options.name: footer
options.description: Content under the starters, such as MonarchAiDisclaimer.

options.name: starters
options.description: Starting points, such as MonarchAiStarterPrompts. The trailing lambda.

states.name: with agent
states.description: The agent's avatar (large, decorative) with its name in the AI strong color and its role after a middle dot.

states.name: without agent
states.description: A 48dp tile in the AI subtle color with the AI border, holding the optional icon.

states.name: with capabilities
states.description: A start-aligned checklist under the description.

appearance: Centered, with the title in the title style and the description in muted body text. The mark uses the AI subtle fill, AI border and AI strong content; the agent's name is in the AI strong color. Capabilities are body text after a muted mark. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Same parts and order as the web and iOS. The web takes a heading level; Android marks the title as a heading. The web draws a bot and a check glyph; Monarch bundles no icons, so the mark's icon and the capability mark are optional slots (a plain AI tile and a dot without them). The agent's picture is a Painter the app loads, not an image address loaded by the component (the web filters unsafe addresses; iOS loads it with AsyncImage). starters is the trailing lambda, after footer, following the Compose convention. The web narrows its padding below 30rem; on Android the column wraps. Experimental: a domain pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The agent is one TalkBack element read as AI assistant: name, role; the avatar and the middle dot are hidden.
The capabilities are a group named What I can help with, one element per capability; the marks are hidden.
Starters and footer keep their own semantics and touch targets.
The title and capabilities wrap at the largest font scale.
edgeCases: A blank description or role is left out.
Long titles wrap and stay centered.
Put the welcome in the conversation's scrolling area; it does not scroll itself.

With capabilities

MonarchAiWelcome(
